Values by cell: fishing effort and the like, chosen by gear, year or any column

Source: R/cells.R
og_cells.Rd

og_cells() colours a table of cells by a value per square kilometre, such as hours of fishing, summed by cell, gear and year. The page has a control for each column the cells are chosen by (all of a gear, one, or several from the address; a span of years), and the colours' own: the palette, the stretch, the floor and the cap on a histogram of the cells in view, fitted to the view. As the page asks for a tile, DuckDB sums the cells under it to about a screen pixel at that zoom, the reader's choices applied; a cell's value is its sum over its area, so a colour holds across zooms. A click on a cell shows its values.

Usage

og_cells(
  map = NULL,
  cells = NULL,
  values = NULL,
  count = "n",
  by = NULL,
  one_of = NULL,
  range = "year",
  unit = 0.001,
  h3 = NULL,
  sizes = c(0.01, 0.05, 0.1, 0.5),
  ices = TRUE,
  pixel = TRUE,
  cell = NULL,
  vessels = NULL,
  min_vessels = 1,
  follow = "vessel",
  gear = NULL,
  filter = list(),
  metric = NULL,
  palette = "magma",
  opacity = 85,
  limits = NULL,
  stretch = c("even", "equal"),
  labels = NULL,
  codes = NULL,
  name = "Cells",
  id = "cells",
  info = NULL,
  section = name,
  visible = TRUE
)

Arguments

map

A map the pipe makes (og_map(), with data or none, and any layer functions). Given the cells instead (or nothing), a map is started for them.

cells

The cells (see The cells).

values, count, by

The columns summed and coloured, the count summed, and those chosen by (see The cells).

one_of

Columns of by whose values are ways of counting the same thing, not parts of it (two definitions of fishing, say): one value shown at a time, the first by default, with no "all".

range

Columns of by chosen as a span of two values, from and to: "year" by default, where there is one.

unit

The degrees of one step of ix and iy.

h3

The column of the cells' H3 index: by default "h3" where the cells have one; FALSE, none.

sizes, ices

The cell sizes in degrees the page offers besides about a pixel, those that are a whole number of the cells' own; ices, whether the ICES statistical rectangle (1 by 0.5 degrees) is one of them. A bundle carries every size offered.

pixel

Whether the page offers cells of about a screen pixel at each zoom (and finer and coarser) beside the fixed sizes. FALSE, the fixed sizes alone (and H3's), opening on the finest: for cells whose own size is already about a pixel at the zooms they are looked at, where a pixel's cells are the finest size's.

cell

The cells' size when the page opens: NULL, about a pixel (the finest size with pixel = FALSE; H3 following the zoom where the cells have no squares); one of sizes; "ices"; "h3", H3 following the zoom; or "h3_<resolution>", such as "h3_9".

vessels

The column of by that names a vessel, for the cells' number of vessels: by default the first of vid, vessel_id, VESSEL_ID, vessel and mmsi there is; FALSE, none.

min_vessels

The fewest vessels a cell shown has when the page opens: 1 (all), 2, 3, 5 or 10.

follow

On a map with a time panel (og_time()) whose groups are the cells' vessels, the cells shown follow the vessel chosen there: "vessel", its own; "gear", its gear's (the gear of most of its first value); or "fleet", all of them. The page's Show changes it; FALSE, no such control. Needs vessels.

gear

The column of by that names a gear, for follow: by default the first of gear, gid, GEAR, gear_code and metier there is.

filter

The choices when the page opens, by column: list(gid = 6, year = c(2015, 2020)), a value or several of a list (several, comma-separated in the address), the first and last of a span. Those not given: all, the whole span, or the first of one_of.

metric

The value coloured when the page opens, one of values.

palette

The colours, one of the map's palettes for a grid (og_palettes()): "magma" by default.

opacity

The cells' opacity, 0-100.

limits

The values per square kilometre the palette's ends stand at, c(floor, cap); by default fitted to the view (the 2nd and 98th percentiles of the cells in view), until the reader sets them.

stretch

How the values are spread over the palette: "even" on a log scale, or "equal", each colour an equal share of the cells in view.

labels

The columns' names as the page shows them, where the file's dictionary has none: a named character vector, column to label (c(gid = "Gear", h = "Hours")); a value's is followed by "per km²".

codes

The names of codes in the columns chosen by, where the file's dictionary has none: a named list by column, each a named vector, code to name (list(gid = c("6" = "Bottom trawl (OTB)"))).

name, info

The layer's name in the sidebar and the text behind its ⓘ.

id

The layer's id, its key in the page's address, and the start of its controls' keys (<id>_<column>).

section

The sidebar's box the layer sits in, by its title.

visible

Whether the cells are on when the page opens.

Value

The map, with the layer. A map has one such layer at most. og_bundle() carries it with no further word, summed by the browser from the cells at sizes from 0.01 degrees up; H3's hexagons are drawn on a served map only, so a bundle offers the squares alone, and leaves out cells that have no squares.

Details

The page's Cells sets their size, live: about a screen pixel at each zoom (finer or coarser), or one size at every zoom (by default 0.01, 0.05, a c-square, 0.1 and 0.5 degrees, and the ICES statistical rectangle, 1 by 0.5 degrees), so the reader sees what a grid's resolution does to the picture. A size narrower than half a pixel at the zoom is drawn at a whole number of it that is not. Where the cells also carry their H3 cell (h3), the same control offers H3's hexagons: at a resolution following the zoom (about eight pixels across), or at one resolution at every zoom, from the cells' own to coarser; a square and a hexagon are two grids over the same values. Where the cells name their vessel (vessels), the page also hides the cells of fewer than a number of vessels chosen there (all by default), as a confidentiality rule would, and a click shows each cell's.

The arguments are the starting look and choices; the page's controls change them, and a value in the page's address wins over both.

The cells

cells is a table with a row for each cell and combination of the columns chosen by, one of:

  • nothing (NULL): the file named by the environment variable OGIS_CELLS, a line in .Renviron (OGIS_CELLS=D:/data/effort.parquet), so a script shared between colleagues carries no path;

  • the path of a Parquet file (or several, a glob), read where it is: a file sorted by the cell's corner reads fastest;

  • a data frame, or a lazy table on DuckDB.

Its columns:

  • ix and iy (or x and y): the cell's south-west corner, in whole steps of unit degrees of longitude and latitude (thousandths of a degree by default). The cells' own size is read from the corners: a table of 0.005-degree cells is drawn no finer than that;

  • h3 (optional, or the column named by h3): the cell's H3 index, as text or a whole number, all of one resolution, the finest drawn. A table may have both a square and an H3 cell on each row (a row for each pair that meets), or either alone. H3 needs DuckDB's community extension h3, installed on first use;

  • values: the columns summed, each coloured per square kilometre; by default every column of fractions;

  • count: a column of whole numbers summed and shown on a click, not coloured (n, the records, by default);

  • by: the columns the reader chooses by, the others by default: each a list of its values ("all" first, then the values by their share of the first value, the largest first), or for a column of years (range) a span of two.

Labels come from the file's data dictionary (data-dict.tidyverse.org's, in the Parquet file's metadata) where it has one: a column's label names its control or its value, and its values name a code (a gear's id as its name); else from codes, else the column's own name.

See also

og_layer()'s "grid", which it makes; og_relief() and og_names(), for a sea floor and its names under it.

Examples

# hours by 0.01-degree cell, gear and year
set.seed(1)
cells <- expand.grid(ix = seq(-24000, -22000, by = 10), iy = seq(65000, 66000, by = 10),
                     gear = c("trawl", "longline"), year = 2020:2022)
cells$hours <- rexp(nrow(cells)) * ifelse(cells$gear == "trawl", 3, 1)
og_cells(cells, labels = c(gear = "Gear", year = "Years", hours = "Hours"), name = "Fishing effort")
#> <og_map> Map
#>   layers: cells (grid)

# trawls in 2021 alone, coloured from 0.5 to 50 hours a km², in blues
og_cells(cells, filter = list(gear = "trawl", year = c(2021, 2021)), limits = c(0.5, 50),
         palette = "blues")
#> <og_map> Map
#>   layers: cells (grid)

# the same hours on H3's hexagons too, beside the squares (each row a square and the hexagon it meets)
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
con <- DBI::dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb())
DBI::dbExecute(con, "INSTALL h3 FROM community; LOAD h3")
duckdb::duckdb_register(con, "cells", cells)
hex <- DBI::dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT ix, iy, h3_latlng_to_cell_string((iy + 5) / 1000, (ix + 5) / 1000, 8) AS h3,
                                    gear, year, hours FROM cells")
og_cells(hex, cell = "h3_7", name = "Fishing effort")
} # }

# cells named once, by OGIS_CELLS in .Renviron, over the sea floor:
# og_map() |> og_relief() |> og_cells(name = "Fishing effort", one_of = "preset")
